card.title: Test a local web app
card.what_it_does: Tests and debugs a local web application using Playwright, capturing screenshots and browser logs to verify functionality.

addyosmani-browser-testing-with-devtools.name: browser-testing-with-devtools

install.claude-ai: Available on paid plans — enable in Settings > Capabilities, then just ask.

nutrition.trigger: Use when building or debugging anything that runs in a browser.

addyosmani-browser-testing-with-devtools.summary: Provides a workflow for using the Chrome DevTools MCP server to test and debug browser-based applications, covering installation via npx chrome-devtools-mcp with isolated or auto-connect Chrome profiles. Documents specific tools for capturing screenshots, inspecting the DOM, reading console logs, monitoring network requests, tracing performance metrics such as Core Web Vitals, checking computed styles, and reading the accessibility tree. Also defines security rules for treating browser content as untrusted data and constraining JavaScript execution to read-only inspection.

adds performance/accessibility/network tracing not present in the other
related.reason: Both debug a locally running web app via browser tooling with screenshots and logs, but rely on different frameworks and one is read-only inspection while the other does interactive functional verification.

addyosmani-test-driven-development.name: test-driven-development

install.claude-ai: Available on paid plans — enable in Settings > Capabilities, then just ask.

nutrition.trigger: Use when implementing any logic, fixing any bug, or changing any behavior.

addyosmani-test-driven-development.summary: Describes the red-green-refactor test-driven development cycle — write a failing test, write minimal code to pass it, then refactor with tests green — and the 'Prove-It Pattern' for bug fixes, which requires writing a reproduction test that fails before implementing any fix. Specifies a test pyramid allocating roughly 80% unit, 15% integration, and 5% end-to-end tests, classifies tests into small/medium/large resource tiers by I/O and process usage, and recommends asserting on outcome state rather than internal method calls, favoring self-contained tests over shared setup helpers.

related.name: testing-strategy
shared_elements: guidance consulted before writing new tests
concerned with test coverage and structure consistency
reference for how tests in a codebase should be written
key_differences: prescribes a universal red-green-refactor cycle and fixed test-pyramid ratios vs adapting to one project's existing conventions
includes a specific bug-fix reproduction pattern not present in the other
opinionated universal methodology vs descriptive project-specific reference
related.reason: Both are pre-writing references meant to shape how new tests get written and kept consistent, but one prescribes a universal methodology while the other reflects a specific project's own conventions.

related.name: webapp-testing
shared_elements: both aim to verify software behaves as expected

governs how tests are written vs runtime verification of an already-running app
framework-agnostic vs tied to a specific automation framework
related.reason: TDD is a generic test-writing methodology while webapp-testing is a specific runtime browser-verification toolkit, overlapping only in the broad goal of confirming correctness.

related.name: triage-flaky-test
shared_elements: both address fixing the underlying cause of a test problem
both concerned with test reliability
key_differences: proactive writing-phase methodology vs reactive post-hoc diagnosis of an existing failure

related.reason: TDD guides how tests get written going forward, while triage-flaky-test reactively diagnoses one already-failing test using historical run data, a different point in the lifecycle.

nutrition.trigger: Use when starting a new session, when agent output quality degrades, when switching between tasks, or when you need to configure rules files and context for a project.

addyosmani-context-engineering.summary: Describes a five-level context hierarchy for AI coding agents, from persistent rules files (CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules, AGENTS.md, GitHub Copilot instructions) down to specs, relevant source files, error output, and conversation history, with guidance on trust levels for each source. Presents context-packing patterns — a full session brain-dump, a selective per-task file list, and a hierarchical project-map summary — and lists MCP servers (Context7, Chrome DevTools, PostgreSQL, filesystem, GitHub) that supply additional context, plus a protocol for surfacing conflicts between spec and existing code instead of silently choosing one.

B actively generates/refreshes the actual CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files plus scaffolds directories

kunalsuri-resumable-sdd.summary: Implements a lightweight spec-driven-development workflow that breaks a multi-step task into a git-committed spec, a derived checklist, and a loop of implement-test-commit-checkoff cycles. It writes docs/SPECS-<feature>.md (context, scope decisions, design, acceptance criteria) as one commit, then derives docs/implementation-<feature>.md as a per-step checklist committed separately. Each step is implemented, run through a test gate, committed, and checked off with a result note in its own commit, so a new session or agent can resume exactly where work stopped by reading just those two files. It points to GitHub Spec Kit for the fuller constitution-to-implementation SDD pipeline this skill deliberately simplifies.
